chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The owner of seven hundred [dirhams] takes the zakat if no one else is found.' I said, 'But the zakat is obligatory upon the owner of seven hundred.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'His zakat is charity upon his dependents, and he does not take it unless he relies entirely on the seven hundred such that it is exhausted in less than a year; this one takes it. And the zakat is not permissible for one who has a profession and possesses wealth upon which zakat is obligatory.'

key_terms.صَاحِبُ السَّبْعِمِائَةِ: Owner of seven hundred [dirhams, the nisab for silver]

ai.seo_question: Can a person who is obligated to pay zakat also receive it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the nuanced Shia jurisprudence regarding the eligibility of the 'poor' (fuqara) to receive zakat while simultaneously owing it, a concept known as 'zakat on one's own zakat.' Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies that an owner of nisab (700 dirhams) may receive zakat only if his wealth is not stable but rather consumed rapidly (within a year), distinguishing him from those with a profession or sufficient fixed assets who are excluded to prevent the concentration of wealth among the elite.
